label: v5 simulator correctness audit (simulator only; NO training, NO performance claim)

bug_fixed_this_audit.summary: A failed range was logged as ONE window sample (failure=1, retry=1, completed=0), while the live runner (policy_runner.observe) records two attempts: a failed attempt and a successful retry attempt (retry=1, completed=1). The simulator now pushes both samples. Bytes were already credited exactly once and elapsed already included the retransmission; those were unchanged.
bug_fixed_this_audit.effect: recent_failure_rate/recent_retry_rate/recent_completed_norm and window attempts now follow the live definition. Elapsed time, bytes, rewards, RNG draw order and the static sweep are unchanged.
bug_fixed_this_audit.consequence_for_existing_candidate: final_dqn_candidate_v5.json was trained BEFORE this fix, on the old window semantic. It is not modified and must not be treated as trained on the corrected state distribution; any further use requires retraining (not done in this task).

verified_semantics: fixed 1 MiB chunk; partial final range credited once
concurrency always within [1,4]; invalid action raises with no state mutation; boundary actions are no-ops
one step = decision_interval requests except the final partial step
C=4 runs 4 requests in parallel (pipeline time = sum(service)/active)
reward == -step elapsed exactly; sum(step elapsed) == episode elapsed
phase selected by elapsed wall-clock time at each request start; transition affects later work in the same step/episode
transition request index depends on per-request timing (time-based, not count-based)
failed range: bytes credited once, elapsed includes one retransmission, windows record failed attempt + successful retry
terminal exactly when done_bytes == total; truncation only from max_episode_steps; finishing on the last allowed step is terminal
randomize()/reset()/step() deterministic for a fixed seed
single-phase episodes never transition; multi-phase episodes transition in >= 50% of sampled episodes
modelled_limitations: a failed request is retransmitted exactly once and the retransmission cannot fail
effective loss is capped at 0.9; loss/congestion are an expected-cost model, not a TCP model
per-extra-connection overhead (0.02 s) and congestion increments are MODELLED, not measured
dedicated real-server C=1..4 completion measurements are UNAVAILABLE; the concurrency relationship is qualitative
no max-retries exhaustion: a request never permanently fails
loss/congestion alone never lowers best C in this model (see attribution: no_cap + loss -> C=4); a lower best C needs a shared bottleneck, so 'loss => fewer connections' is NOT a modelled rule

calibration.interpretation: The simulator is an ideal pacing model (bytes/rate); the real server adds fixed per-request HTTP/pacing overhead of ~50 ms. The gap is recorded, not fitted; full simulator fidelity is NOT claimed.

static_sweep_note: Variation in best fixed C comes from the simulator mechanics: shared bottleneck vs per-response throttle (link_bandwidth/rate), latency overlap, and loss/congestion + per-connection overhead. No optimal-C rule is hard-coded. These are modelled behaviors, not real-server evidence.
